summary:
BLACK HOLE ECHO is a software-based astronomy project that explores gravitational lensing through computational modelling. It aims to simulate how light from distant sources is bent by the gravity of massive foreground objects and reconstruct selected lens properties, including the lens centre and Einstein radius, from simulated observations.

The software combines a gravitational-lensing simulator, image reconstruction algorithms, noise testing and visual analysis in an interactive dashboard. It compares estimated parameters with known values to evaluate reconstruction accuracy and investigates how noise and incomplete image data affect the results.

The project makes complex astronomical concepts more accessible through interactive experimentation using a computer. It also demonstrates how mathematical modelling, scientific computing and image analysis can help us study astronomical phenomena that cannot be investigated directly in a classroom.
details:
Project Details — BLACK HOLE ECHO

BLACK HOLE ECHO is a software-based computational astronomy project designed to demonstrate gravitational lensing and reconstruct the apparent geometry of a gravitational lens from simulated observations.

How does it work?

The application generates a synthetic astronomical image using a mathematical lensing model. It simulates an extended background light source whose apparent position is altered by the gravitational influence of a foreground lens. Adjustable parameters allow users to change the lens centre, Einstein radius and image noise.

The reconstruction engine processes the generated image, searches for bright annular arc patterns and estimates the apparent lens centre and Einstein radius. Users can compare these estimates with the original simulation parameters and calculate reconstruction errors. A blind-test mode allows the known parameters to remain hidden until the user chooses to reveal them.

Tools and technologies

The project is developed using Python and Streamlit. NumPy supports numerical calculations, SciPy provides image processing and numerical optimization functions, and Matplotlib is used for scientific visualization. The application runs on a standard computer without requiring physical controllers or electronic hardware.

Benefits and intended impact

BLACK HOLE ECHO aims to make gravitational lensing easier to understand through interactive computational experimentation. It connects physics, mathematics, image processing and programming in an accessible educational tool. It also demonstrates how mathematical models can be used to investigate astronomical phenomena and evaluate the reliability of computational estimates.

Creativity and development considerations

The project combines a gravitational-lensing simulation, automatic geometric reconstruction, adjustable noise and blind testing in one interactive application. Important development considerations include mathematical consistency, numerical stability, image quality, reconstruction error and the limitations of simplified physical models.

The current version uses synthetic observations and a simplified softened radial lens model. It is an educational reconstruction prototype, not a black-hole detection system. Future development will focus on independent experimental validation, incomplete-image testing, uncertainty analysis and comparison with suitable real astronomical observations.
